jurisdiction.name: Oman
jurisdiction.overview: Oman governs AI through MTCIT policy instruments and the Personal Data Protection Law; GCC and UNESCO instruments are shown separately as regional records.

narrative.summary: Oman governs AI through policy instruments issued by the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology (MTCIT), backed by binding data protection law; there is no AI-specific statute. The National Program for AI and Advanced Digital Technologies, approved by the Council of Ministers on 19 September 2024, sets the strategy under the National Program for Digital Economy and Oman Vision 2040. It replaced the 2022 Executive Program. The General Policy for the Safe and Ethical Use of AI Systems (April 2025), drafted after a public consultation in August 2024, sets mandatory controls and ethical principles for government units and regulated private institutions. It updates the narrower 2021 AI Systems Policy for government. The Personal Data Protection Law (Royal Decree 6/2022) and its 2024 Executive Regulation are the binding layer; Royal Decree 68/2026 added a right to object to automated decisions and a duty to give contested decisions human review. In April 2026 Royal Decree 50/2026 created an AI Special Zone in Muscat, but no official full text could be retrieved, so it is kept as a lead.

instruments.summary: MTCIT's national AI policy setting technical controls and ethical principles for using and developing AI systems across the lifecycle. It applies to all government units and to private institutions regulated by sector regulators. Users must provide human oversight of sensitive decisions, explain decisions in high-impact uses such as employment, health and finance, and hand documentation to regulators on request. Developers must assess ethical, social and environmental impact before deployment, label or watermark generative AI output, test for bias and follow cybersecurity practice. MTCIT monitors state units and reports to the Council of Ministers; each sector regulator monitors its own sector.

instruments.summary: Oman's national AI programme, updating the 2022 Executive Program into a comprehensive programme under the National Program for Digital Economy and Oman Vision 2040. It rests on three pillars: adoption of AI in economic and development sectors, localisation of AI technologies, and human-centred AI governance (including updating legislation, e.g. copyright for generative AI, and an international centre for AI ethics). Implementation is overseen by the Council of Ministers' Financial and Economic Committee and the Digital Economy Technical Committee, with MTCIT responsible for legislation, oversight and follow-up.

instruments.current_status: Royal Decree 6/2022 signed 9 February 2022 and published in Official Gazette No. 1429 (MTCIT gives 13 February 2022). Article 4 of the decree brings the law into force one year after publication, hence 13 February 2023 (computed). Amended by Royal Decree 68/2026 (Official Gazette No. 1664, September 2026), which adds rules on automated processing. MTCIT is the competent authority.
instruments.summary: Oman's general data protection law, administered by MTCIT. It requires the data subject's express consent for processing, gives data subjects rights to withdraw consent, correct, update and erase data and to be notified of breaches, and sets controller and processor obligations with fines. It governs personal data used to train and run AI systems; since the 2026 amendment it also contains specific automated-processing provisions (Article 14).

instruments.issuing_authority: Sultanate of Oman (Sultan, by Royal Decree)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology (MTCIT)
instruments.current_status: Signed 3 September 2026 and published in Official Gazette No. 1664; MTCIT lists 6 September 2026. Article 3 brings it into force the day after publication, hence 7 September 2026 (computed). Amendment text checked against the MTCIT gazette PDF and a non-official transcription.
instruments.summary: Amends the Personal Data Protection Law: it extends the law to processing of data of natural persons in Oman wherever processing takes place, revises exemptions and consent exceptions, and adds a definition of automated processing. New Article 14 requires controllers and processors using automated processing to protect privacy and avoid harm, gives data subjects a right to object to decisions resulting from automated processing, and requires human review of contested decisions, with fines of OMR 5,000-10,000 for breaches.

instruments.summary: Oman's first policy regulating AI use by government administrative units. It sets six principles (inclusiveness, human-centred, accountability, fairness, transparency, safety) and 19 mandatory terms, including risk assessments, bias checks, internal audits, explainability, logging, pre-production testing, disclaimers to affected people and consent for high-impact automated decisions. MTCIT audits compliance and reports to the Council of Ministers.

coverage_audit.technical_note:
Method note (original): Deep review completed on 6 October 2026. All records were read on Ministry of Transport, Communications and IT pages or documents; the two earlier records were corrected and one was re-linked to the ministry's own copy. The official legal portal could not be read, so the gazette details for two royal decrees and a ministry circular could not be confirmed there. A ministry page on a 2025 AI strategy is no longer online and was not recorded. Effective dates for the data protection law and its 2026 amendment are worked out from their commencement articles.

Coverage note (original): No AI-specific instrument was found from the Cyber Defence Centre / Oman National CERT, the Projects, Tenders and Local Content Authority, the national standards directorate (DGSM at the Ministry of Commerce), the Central Bank of Oman, the Financial Services Authority, the TRA, or the Ministries of Health and Education. The 2025 General Policy itself covers cybersecurity, risk assessment and generative AI. No AI-specific sandbox or government AI index was found. MTCIT's annual report cites the Oxford Insights index, which is not a government index. No national treaty instrument was found; GCC and UNESCO instruments come from data/regional. Technical review notes: Deep review 2026-10-06. All recorded instruments were read on official MTCIT pages or PDFs (mtcit.gov.om library, AI sector publications page, and the legacy ITAPortal). The 2025 General Policy PDF is image-only (Canva) and was read page by page. The two domain-named organisations were merged into one MTCIT organisation. qanoon.om (non-official legal portal) was used only to discover and cross-check gazette numbers and dates (Royal Decree 68/2026: Official Gazette 1664, 6 Sep 2026; Royal Decree 50/2026: Official Gazette 1646, 4 May 2026; MTCIT Circular 11/2025 of 9 Apr 2025). Effective dates for the PDPL (13 Feb 2023) and Royal Decree 68/2026 (7 Sep 2026) are calculated from the commencement articles and the MTCIT publication dates. leads.title: مرسوم سلطاني رقم 50/2026 بإنشاء منطقة الذكاء الاصطناعي الخاصة في محافظة مسقط
leads.english_title: Royal Decree No. 50/2026 establishing the Artificial Intelligence Special Zone in Muscat Governorate
leads.note: Signed 30 April 2026; Official Gazette No. 1646 (4 May 2026) according to the non-official qanoon.om transcription. It creates a special economic zone for AI, and the Public Authority for Special Economic Zones and Free Zones appoints its operator in coordination with MTCIT. mjla.gov.om was unreachable (TLS error / HTTP 503) and OPAZ carries only a news item. Promote this lead once an official full text is reachable.

leads.title: تعميم رقم 11/2025 بشأن السياسة العامة للاستخدام الآمن والأخلاقي لأنظمة الذكاء الاصطناعي
leads.english_title: MTCIT Circular No. 11/2025 on the General Policy for the Safe and Ethical Use of AI Systems
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology (MTCIT)
leads.note: Dated 9 April 2025, signed by the Minister. It directs state administrative units and regulated private institutions to comply with the policy, including for generative AI. Seen only on qanoon.om; no official copy was found on mtcit.gov.om. If an official copy is found, add it to i-36ee3b354e09 as the effective date.

leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology (MTCIT)
leads.note: The consultation draft was published for comment from 2 to 31 August 2024. The MTCIT consultation page now links only to the results report (recorded as i-fc3cb66142f3), not to the draft text.

leads.title: دليل ممارسات الذكاء الاصطناعي في العملية التعليمية
leads.english_title: Guide to Artificial Intelligence Practices in the Educational Process
leads.note: Ministry of Education guide for teachers, supervisors and school administrations on using AI in schools: central team for a national programme on AI in school education, reporting to the ministry's digital transformation committee, security controls (use only ministry-approved applications, protect personal data, no sharing of confidential information, prior consent when AI depicts real persons) and a risk section. Issuance reported by Oman Daily on 24 December 2024 (discovery only). The ministry's site (moe.gov.om, home.moe.gov.om) refused connections or returned HTTP 503 on 2026-10-13, so no official text or stated date was seen. Promote once an official copy is reachable; likely administrative_guideline (sectoral, generative-ai, public-sector).

leads.title: الإطار العام لإدماج الذكاء الاصطناعي والتقنيات المتقدمة في التعليم
leads.english_title: General Framework for Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technologies in Education
leads.note: Ministry of Education framework document described as a national reference for integrating AI and advanced technologies into the school system and curricula (reported by Oman Daily on 3 August 2026; Times of Oman on 6 September 2026 says the ministry will begin implementing an AI framework for school education in the 2026/2027 academic year, covering responsible AI use, teacher training, digital literacy and pilots). Discovery only; the ministry's site was unreachable on 2026-10-13, so no official text or stated date was seen. Check scope on reading: it may be mainly a curriculum-integration document rather than one that sets expectations for AI use.

leads.title: سياسة الذكاء الاصطناعي - وزارة العمل
leads.english_title: Ministry of Labour Artificial Intelligence Policy
leads.note: Reported in the UNESCO AI Readiness Assessment (RAM) report on Oman (2026) as 'under official approval'; the Ministry of Labour is also Oman's civil-service authority, so this may be public-servant AI policy. No document found on mol.gov.om (homepage, ministerial decisions and regulations pages searched 2026-10-13). Official title not known; the title here is descriptive. Promote once the ministry publishes it.
